=== B3 (BLOCKING, measured, and NEW since the last review). The state-claims check is red again, by the exact ordering trap the repository documented. ===
    python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py   ->  exit 1

    f9b4deadbb441f0c1046a0d73b0434424f1cf13c (live: bfe850796969980545811e1ffa551b9143965faf)
ci.yml runs this script. The reviewer at ae29b1a9 verified this same check exited 0 and called the "regenerate LAST" ordering fix correct. It WAS correct at that moment. It is not a durable fix: the generated block pins a main SHA, so every merge into main re-breaks it, and this branch has been open across at least two such merges. The fix that would hold is to stop pinning a volatile SHA in a committed block, or to regenerate it in CI rather than by hand. I am recording this as a defect in the approach, not as a regression by the author.
I NEARLY GOT THIS WRONG IN THE OTHER DIRECTION AND AM PRINTING IT: my first pass ran the gate scripts in a shell loop that piped each to `tail`, so the exit status I read was `tail`'s, not the script's. That loop reported exit=0 for all four and I would have recorded "gates pass". I caught it, re-ran capturing the true status, and only then charged B2 and B3. A checker whose own harness cannot tell a failure from a pass is precisely the shape this PR's own tests are about.

=== B4 (BLOCKING, code defect in this PR, PROVED BY MUTATION). scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py counts a review record that names NO commit. ===
review_records() does:
    reviewed = str(record.get("reviewed_commit", ""))
    ...
    if not head.startswith(reviewed):
A missing or empty reviewed_commit becomes "", and every string starts with "". So a record with no reviewed_commit at all -- or a one-character one -- passes the freshness test and is counted by the ARMED MERGE PATH as a satisfied independent review.
REPRODUCTION, driving this PR's own FakeRepo harness against the real aq.readiness (probe kept out of the tree):
    A. unmutated good record                   -> ready=True   (harness sane)
    B. reviewed_commit key REMOVED             -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    C. reviewed_commit = ""                    -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    D. reviewed_commit = one character         -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    E. reviewed_commit = a wrong 40-char sha   -> ready=False, "reviewed_commit deadbeefdead is not this head"
E is the control: the probe is not vacuous; the check does refuse a genuinely wrong sha. B/C/D are the hole. The schema calls reviewed_commit required with pattern ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$, but lwb_auto_queue.py does not load the schema -- lwb_lanes.py does. The armed path has its own, weaker, copy of the rule. First reported at 8a839703; re-proved here.

=== B5 (BLOCKING, code defect in this PR, PROVED AGAINST LIVE DATA). The armed merge gate is unsatisfiable by an honest record, and I did not need a synthetic case to show it. ===
review_records() compares the record against data["head"]["sha"] from the pulls API -- the RAW head. But a review record is COMMITTED, and that commit advances the raw head past the sha the record names. scripts/lwb_lanes.py handles this with resolve_reviewable_head, which skips commits touching only reviews/ and proof/. lwb_auto_queue.py has no such step.
LIVE PROOF, using another open pull request rather than a fixture -- PR #38 carries two records with verdict AGREE naming 57f130ab92c7dff0aa5d5fce5b13e52a1a4a059c, which IS its reviewable head:
    aq.review_records(38, "4d667eb246e2665804563d90857019a9443f7017")
    -> good = 0
       reviews/38/cloud-reviewer-b.json: reviewed_commit 57f130ab92c7 is not this head
       reviews/38/cloud-reviewer.json:   reviewed_commit 57f130ab92c7 is not this head
So a pull request the repository's own lane gate treats as fully reviewed is refused by the armed merge path, 0 of 1. B4 and B5 together are the worse shape: the gate refuses every honest record and accepts one that names nothing.
Both were reported before me (B5 at ae29b1a9); what is new here is that B5 is now demonstrable against real records on a real open pull request, not only a harness.

=== N1 (NON-BLOCKING, mine, not reproduced). check_conclusions relies on an ordering the API does not promise. ===
    out.setdefault(name.strip(), conclusion.strip())
    # Latest run for a name wins; the API returns newest first.
The list-check-runs-for-a-ref endpoint does not document a newest-first order. If the order ever differs, a stale green run would mask a fresh red one for the same check name. Sorting by started_at/completed_at and taking the newest would remove the assumption. I did NOT reproduce a wrong-order response; I am recording the assumption, not charging a measured defect.

=== N2 (NON-BLOCKING, mine). Required contexts are read from the ruleset but matched only against check RUNS. ===
required_contexts() returns nine contexts; check_conclusions reads only commits/<sha>/check-runs. A required context posted through the commit Statuses API rather than as a check run would never appear, and would be reported as "has not reported" -- which REFUSES rather than passes. It fails closed, so it is not a hole; it is a latent confusion between two sibling sources. Worth a comment in the script.
